title: Manifestation & Luck / The Mandela Effect
excerpt: Psychologist Joe Gallenberger discussed his pioneering work in manifestation and luck techniques. Followed by Cheryll Jones' interview with metaphysics researcher Aage Nost on the Mandela Effect.
content:
In the first half of our live Thanksgiving night broadcast, clinical psychologist and author Dr. Joe Gallenberger discussed his pioneering work in manifestation, psychokinesis (PK), and mind-matter interaction, along with success stories from his luck techniques. He emphasized the power of focused, coherent thought combined with strong positive emotion in shaping reality. Manifestation, he continued, is a dynamic interplay within a “constant soup” of competing intentions from ourselves and others, but deliberate energy focus can significantly increase one’s influence on life events.

Addressing negativity, Gallenberger said it tends to steer outcomes away from desired goals and can trigger self-fulfilling cycles that impact health and relationships. He illustrated how negative expectations surrounding decisions like investing or relationships can alter behavior and timing, ultimately undermining success. However, he cautioned against “toxic positivity,” or forced optimism that invalidates genuine emotions, advocating instead for authentic gratitude that acknowledges both hardship and blessing.

Speaking of his ongoing work teaching manifestation and PK through workshops, including virtual “Inner Vegas” sessions, he said participants consistently beat statistical odds (like throwing doubles in dice games) by a wide margin. He also delved into his concept of "liquid luck," a meditation and mindset practice designed to foster synchronicity and positive outcomes in life. Sharing compelling examples, like a woman who won $94,000 at slot machines after a spirit-guided intuition, he revealed that liquid luck is about cultivating positive emotions —happiness, abundance, gratitude, compassion— and mentally “drinking” this imaginary elixir to invite serendipity and courage.

---------

In the latter half, C2C's investigative reporter Cheryll Jones presented her recorded interview with metaphysics researcher and futurist Aage Nost on the Mandela Effect and its deeper connections to quantum mechanics, timelines, and collective consciousness. The Mandela Effect, named after the widespread false memory that Nelson Mandela died in prison in the 1980s, is described by Nost as “much more common today and touches far more aspects of our lives than people even realize.” Linking the effect to the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, he explained that “the quantum state of mind is based on probability" and “time is a progression of present moments in the form of mental images stacked one after another.” We can slip between these “frames of time,” causing shifts between timelines, which may explain collective false memories, he added.

He discussed common Mandela Effect examples, such as the disputed Fruit of the Loom logo featuring a cornucopia, which the company maintains never existed — yet according to Nost, physical evidence and old advertisements prove otherwise. He posits that these phenomena indicate humanity exists within “fluid mind-created simulations” or parallel universes, an idea aligned with the many-worlds theory and scientific equations suggesting a 93% probability that reality is a simulation.

Nost asserted that individuals can influence their own timelines through thought and action, citing his personal experience of changing his life path from farming in Norway to becoming a professional pilot in the United States. Addressing the power of consciousness, he suggested individuals can influence their timelines through focused visualization and positive intention. “You start creating a new reality for yourself in your mind... You take that ball of energy and you place it into the future,” he explained, advocating meditation and association with spiritually successful individuals to raise one’s vibration. During the third hour, he joined George and Cheryll live for questions.

In the final half-hour, George presented a tribute to recently deceased physicist Russell Targ, featuring an interview excerpt from the 7/13/23 show.

News segment guests: Jeff Nelken, Kevin Randle
